chapter_title: The Seventh, concerning the Five Fathers
chapter_note: This chapter’s oldest layer is a structured emanation schema: five “fathers” emerging one from another, with triadic evocations (Father → three; Third Ambassador → three; Jesus the Splendour → three; Light Mind → three), in an impersonal cosmological voice. In the second half, the register drifts toward ecclesial/institutional identifications (apostle/church/elect/catechumens) and a closing beatitude; one paragraph embeds a Johannine saying (Jn 8), which is a Christian overlay.

paragraphs.temporal_note: Hagiographic sitting/preaching scene with titles (“enlightener… apostle of truth”) and revelation-introduction; pure compilation frame.

paragraphs.core_text: Five fathers exist; they were summoned forth one of one. [Also], one did come out of another!
paragraphs.temporal_note: Numbered cosmological taxonomy stated as an impersonal structural axiom (emanation sequence).

paragraphs.core_text: The first Father is the Father of Greatness, the blessed one of glory, the [on]e who has no measure to his greatness; who also is the first only-begotten, the first eternal; who exists with fiv[e fa]thers for ever; the one who exists before every thing that has existed, and that will exist.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Systematic cosmological epithets and timeless ontological predicates; no institutional application or citation.

paragraphs.core_text: Now he, the glorious Father, summoned from him three emanations. The [fi]rst is the Gre[at] Spirit, the first Mother, who came out of the Father. She appeared first. ⟨p.35⟩
paragraphs.temporal_note: Core emanation mechanics (summoning/emanations) with named divinity; impersonal expository voice.

paragraphs.core_text: The seco[nd i]s the Belo[ved of] the Lights, the great glorious Beloved, [the one w]ho is honour[ed; w]ho came out of the Father. [He ma]nifested ou[t of h]im.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Continues the internal emanation list; despite elevated devotional adjectives, it remains cosmos→cosmos (being-from-being).

paragraphs.core_text: The third father is the Thir[d Ambassador], the eldest of [a]]] the counsell[ors; who came out of] the first Father. He appeared.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Named cosmological hypostasis within the emanation sequence; formulaic but not ecclesial.

paragraphs.core_text: This is the first Father, the first power, the one from whom the three great powers came out. This is the first Father, the first eternal, the root of all the lights; from whom the three emanations came out. They have humiliated the Darkness. They have brought its heart's desire to naught. They have given themselves the victory. They have also given the victory to their aeons.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Cosmic conflict/result language (“humiliated the Darkness”) stays within the mythic system; no address to church or audience.

paragraphs.core_text: The second father, who came out of the first Father, is the Third Ambassador, the model of the King of lights. And again, he too summoned and sent out of him three powers.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Structured iteration (father → three powers) in cosmological terms; internal hierarchy mapping.

paragraphs.core_text: One is the Pillar of Glory, the Perfect Man; the one who bears up under all things; the great Pillar of blessing; the great porter, who is greater than all the porters.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Cosmic office/titles in a catalogue style; no institutional reach.

paragraphs.core_text: The second is glorious Jesus the Splendour; [the] one through whom shall be given life eternal.
paragraphs.temporal_note: “Jesus the Splendour” here functions as a named cosmological power within a triad; not a Gospel citation formula, so best read as the system’s Jesus-hypostasis (core), though the “life eternal” phrasing is later-sounding.

paragraphs.core_text: The third is the Virgin of Light, the glorious wisd[o]m; the one who takes away the heart of the [rul]ers and the powers by her image, as she fulfils the pleas[u]re of the greatness.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Mythic agency of a Light-being acting upon cosmic “rulers and powers”; internal system mechanics (image/power) rather than church application.

paragraphs.core_text: The third father, who came out of the second father: he is glorious Jesus the Splendour. And, again, he too summoned three evocations after the pattern of the second father.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Explicit recursive patterning (“after the pattern…”) is characteristic of the older schematic teaching layer.

paragraphs.core_text: The first power whom he summoned is the Light Min[d],
paragraphs.removed_material: Removed institutional/ecclesial application: “the father of all the apostles, the eldest of [a]ll the [ch]urches; the one whom Jesus has appointed corresponding to our pattern in the holy church.” This pivots from naming a cosmic power to mapping it onto church offices and the contemporary ‘holy church’.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Opens as a cosmological list-item (name of a power), then crosses boundary cosmos→institution (“apostles… churches… holy church”), indicating later editorial application.

paragraphs.core_text: The second power whom Jesus summo[n]ed is the gre[at Jud]ge, who gives judgement on all the souls of mankind, [his] dwelling being established in the atmosphere under [ ... / ... ] wheel [ ... ] stars.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Cosmic geography (“atmosphere… wheel… stars”) and functional role (judge) remain within the system; no citation or ecclesial address.

Contains a Johannine-style dominical saying (“what I have seen with my Father…”) and “the savio[ur]” language; this entered via NT/Gospel tradition (Jn 8 in apparatus), not the older schematic substrate.

paragraphs.core_text: The fourth father is the Light Mind. And, again, he too summoned three powers after the pattern of Jesus.
paragraphs.removed_material: Removed institutional phrase: “the one who chooses all the churches.” This applies the cosmic figure directly to church selection/administration.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Core is the continued numbered emanation schema; the ‘churches’ clause signals later ecclesial reuse of the pattern.
Institutional/apostolic office language (“Apostle of Light… assume the church of the flesh… leader”) frames salvation history in church terms rather than cosmic architecture.
Continues ecclesial/missionary apparatus (“counterpart… to the apostle… companion… help”), not a cosmos→cosmos mapping.
Seam-flagged institutional graft: “elect and catechumens… renounce the world” is explicit community discipline/application.

paragraphs.core_text: And also the fifth father is this Light Form; the one who shall appear to everyone who will go out from his body; and the thr[ee] great glorious angels who are come with her.
paragraphs.removed_material: Removed institutional correspondence clause: “corresponding to the pattern of the image to the apostle;” which uses the cosmological event to validate an apostolic/church pattern.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Core is an eschatological/cosmological manifestation (Light Form + three angels). The ‘apostle’ correspondence is a later institutional anchoring.

paragraphs.core_text: One (angel) ho[ld]s the prize in his hand. The second bears the light garment. The third is the one who possesses the diadem and the wreath and the crown of light. These are the three angels of light, the ones who shall come with this Light Form;
paragraphs.removed_material: Removed institutional audience-targeting: “and they appear with her to the elect and the catechumens.” This shifts from describing what the angels ARE/BEAR to identifying contemporary community recipients.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Mostly pure correspondential listing (objects/regalia borne by angelic powers). Final clause applies it to elect/catechumens, marking later pastoral insertion.

paragraphs.core_text: These are the five fathers who have come out of one another. They have appeared and man[ifes]ted through one another!
paragraphs.temporal_note: Closes the schematic emanation chain in the same impersonal, structural voice as the opening axiom.
Beatitude/exhortational closure with salvation reward language (“Blessed is he… righteous… faithful… doers of good things”); late paraenesis rather than schematic cosmology.
